title: Reading a Payslip
blurb: Gross, net and every line in between.
cards: Your payslip lists gross pay at the top, then deductions such as income tax and pension or social contributions, and finally net pay. Check it every month, because mistakes happen.
Which number should you compare against your budget?
Your budget runs on money that actually arrives: net pay.
A pension or social contribution on your payslip is money lost forever.
Those contributions fund your future income, and many employers add their own on top.
Hourly pay depends on hours worked. A salary is a fixed yearly amount split into pay periods. Overtime is often paid at a higher rate, so check how your workplace handles extra hours.
You earn 12 an hour and work 30 hours. What is your gross pay for the week?
Your payslip shows 40 less than you expected. What is the best first step?
Check each deduction against your contract and ask payroll
Ask payroll to explain each line. Errors are common and fixable.
example: A payslip shows $2,500 gross pay and $400 in deductions. Your take-home amount is $2,100, which is the amount to start a monthly spending plan with.
